\section[\texorpdfstring{\ja{ともだち} (tomodachi)}{ともだち (tomodachi)}]{\ja{ともだち} (tomodachi) — a friend}

\label{lesson:JA-C25-tomodachi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Japanese for a son, then the Japanese for a daughter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ja{ともだち}}
\textbf{\ja{ともだち}} — \emph{tomodachi} — \textquotedblleft{}a friend\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ja{ともだち}} (\emph{tomodachi}) is a native compound, inherited rather than borrowed: \emph{tomo}, \textquotedblleft{}companion\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-dachi}, the plural ending \emph{-tachi} voiced, so it was once a plural, \textquotedblleft{}companions\textquotedblright{} (JMdict, KANJIDIC2).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tomodachi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{tomodachi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Japanese for a son, then the Japanese for a daughter, then say \emph{tomodachi} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ja{おとこ} (otoko)}{おとこ (otoko)}]{\ja{おとこ} (otoko) — a man}

\label{lesson:JA-C25-otoko}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Japanese for a friend, then the Japanese for an adult.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ja{おとこ}}
\textbf{\ja{おとこ}} — \emph{otoko} — \textquotedblleft{}a man\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ja{おとこ}} (\emph{otoko}) is a native Japanese word, inherited rather than borrowed from Chinese, and its older origin is not settled. Its kanji was attached to it later as a kun'yomi, a native reading given to a Chinese character (JMdict, KANJIDIC2).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ja{せんせい} (sensei)}{せんせい (sensei)}]{\ja{せんせい} (sensei) — a teacher}

\label{lesson:JA-C25-sensei}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Japanese for a man, then the Japanese for a woman.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ja{せんせい}}
\textbf{\ja{せんせい}} — \emph{sensei} — \textquotedblleft{}a teacher\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ja{せんせい}} (\emph{sensei}) is Sino-Japanese (kango): two Chinese characters read with their on'yomi, readings borrowed from Chinese. They are \emph{sen}, \textquotedblleft{}first, before\textquotedblright{} (Middle Chinese \emph{sen}) and \emph{sei}, \textquotedblleft{}life, birth\textquotedblright{} (\emph{srjaeng}) (Unihan, KANJIDIC2; Middle Chinese after Baxter–Sagart). Read literally, it is \textquotedblleft{}born before\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}
